title: Draft: Deprecate "ws_in4_addr" typedef
description:
Deprecated this type. It is confusing because it is never completely
obvious the byte order being used, despite being network byte order
by convention, and there are many uses of ws_in4_addr that look
wrong or at least dubious. The name also lacks the "_t" suffix
that is conventionally used.

Rename it to ws_in4n_addr_t, the extra "n" standing for network byte-order.

Sometimes it is also useful to allow host byte order, and a generalized
practice, so we add a twin type ws_in4h_addr_t, the "h" standing for host byte-order.

This way the byte order used or expected should never be in question.

This is part of an effort to remove IPv4 address variables and argument declarations
everywhere as integers.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12810/diffs?diff_id=828457681&start_sha=68bfafdb60dc43a9624fd3c0604f48371de3f5b8)
Just renaming some types is not ambitious enough. Replaced with !12844.

changes_data.diff:
@@ -109,6 +109,10 @@ Too many other protocol updates have been made to list them all here.
 * Plugins should provide a `plugin_describe()` function that returns an ORed
   list of flags consisting of the plugin types used (declared in wsutil/plugins.h).
 
+* The `ws_in4_addr` type is deprecated and should not be used anymore.
+  Use the host and network byte-ordered alternatives instead, `ws_in4h_addr_t`
+  and `ws_in4n_addr_t` respectively.
+
 == Getting Wireshark
 
 Wireshark source code and installation packages are available from

@@ -58,7 +58,7 @@ enum ftenum {
 	FT_ETHER,
 	FT_BYTES,
 	FT_UINT_BYTES,
-	FT_IPv4,
+	FT_IPv4,	/* IPv4, in host byte order, with mask */
 	FT_IPv6,
 	FT_IPXNET,
 	FT_FRAMENUM,	/* a UINT32, but if selected lets you go to frame with that number */

@@ -44,7 +44,7 @@ ip_get_subnet_mask(const guint32 mask_length)
  */
 
 int
-tvb_get_ipv4_addr_with_prefix_len(tvbuff_t *tvb, int offset, ws_in4_addr *addr,
+tvb_get_ipv4_addr_with_prefix_len(tvbuff_t *tvb, int offset, ws_in4n_addr_t *addr,
     guint32 prefix_len)
 {
 	guint8 addr_len;

@@ -36,7 +36,7 @@ extern "C" {
 typedef enum {
     AT_NONE,               /* no link-layer address */
     AT_ETHER,              /* MAC (Ethernet, 802.x, FDDI) address */
-    AT_IPv4,               /* IPv4 */
+    AT_IPv4,               /* IPv4, in network byte order */
     AT_IPv6,               /* IPv6 */
     AT_IPX,                /* IPX */
     AT_FC,                 /* Fibre Channel */

@@ -10,30 +10,32 @@
 #ifndef __INET_IPV4_H__
 #define __INET_IPV4_H__
 
-#include <inttypes.h>
-#include <glib.h>
+#include <wireshark.h>
 
-typedef uint32_t ws_in4_addr;	/* 32 bit IPv4 address, in network byte order */
+WS_DEPRECATED_X("Use byte-ordered typedefs instead")
+typedef uint32_t ws_in4_addr;	/* 32 bit IPv4 address, in network byte order (deprecated) */
 
-/*
- * We define these in *network byte order*, unlike the C library. Therefore
- * it uses a different prefix than INADDR_* to make the distinction more obvious.
- */
-#define WS_IN4_LOOPBACK ((ws_in4_addr)GUINT32_TO_BE(0x7f000001))
+typedef uint32_t ws_in4n_addr_t;    /* 32 bit IPv4 address, in network byte order */
+
+typedef uint32_t ws_in4h_addr_t;    /* 32 bit IPv4 address, in host byte order */
+
+#define ws_in4hton(addr)    g_htonl(addr)
+
+#define ws_in4ntoh(addr)    g_ntohl(addr)
 
 /**
  * Unicast Local
  * Returns true if the address is in the 224.0.0.0/24 local network
  * control block
  */
-#define in4_addr_is_local_network_control_block(addr) \
+#define ws_in4h_addr_is_local_network_control_block(addr) \
   ((addr & 0xffffff00) == 0xe0000000)
 
 /**
  * Multicast
  * Returns true if the address is in the 224.0.0.0/4 network block
  */
-#define in4_addr_is_multicast(addr) \
+#define ws_in4h_addr_is_multicast(addr) \
   ((addr & 0xf0000000) == 0xe0000000)
 
 /**
@@ -42,7 +44,7 @@ typedef uint32_t ws_in4_addr;	/* 32 bit IPv4 address, in network byte order */
  * for private IPv4 addresses by section 3 of RFC 1918, namely:
  * 10/8, 172.16/12, and 192.168/16
  */
-#define in4_addr_is_private(addr) \
+#define ws_in4h_addr_is_private(addr) \
   (((addr & 0xff000000) == 0x0a000000) || \
    ((addr & 0xfff00000) == 0xac100000) || \
    ((addr & 0xffff0000) == 0xc0a80000))
@@ -51,7 +53,7 @@ typedef uint32_t ws_in4_addr;	/* 32 bit IPv4 address, in network byte order */
  * Link-local address
  * Returns true if the address is in the 169.254/16 network block
  */
-#define in4_addr_is_link_local(addr) \
+#define ws_in4h_addr_is_link_local(addr) \
   ((addr & 0xffff0000) == 0xa9fe0000)
 
 #endif

commits_data.title: wsutil/inet_addr: Replace deprecated usage of "ws_in4_addr"
commits_data.message:
wsutil/inet_addr: Replace deprecated usage of "ws_in4_addr"

Also add some utility macros to convert IPv4 address byte order,
that currently just rename the GLib macros.
